- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 10% of spike magnitude.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 30d horizon — if forecast is >75 and true is <74, adjust downward by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment history includes 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), model tends to lag — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If forecast is >76 and true is <74, apply “overshoot penalty” — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- For 30d horizon, if forecast is >75 and true is <73, consider “reversion to mean” — adjust downward by 2–4% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
